newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WI sees Australia 96/97 wool forecast rising.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WI sees Australia 96/97 wool forecast rising.

text.p: Indications were that Australia's 1996/97 forecast shorn wool production could soon be raised, statutory authority Wool International (WI) said.
The current estimate was that shorn wool production would fall to 641 million kg in 1996/97 from an estimated 646 million kg in 1995/96, it said in its November Insight publication.
The next Australian Wool Production Forecasting Committee (AWPFC) meeting would be held on November 28, it said .
However, since the last AWPFC meeting, the Australian Bureau of Statistics had raised its estimate of sheep numbers, which are used as a base in forecasting wool production, WI said.
Opening sheep numbers for 1996/97 were estimnated at about three million head higher than for 1995/96 rather than a marginal decline as previously indicated, it said.
"This increase combined with above average seasonal conditions in many areas could lead to a higher level of wool production in 1996/97 than in 1995/96," WI said.
WI also said it was likely that some rundown in grower stocks was occurring.
An increase to 856,463 bales of wool-in-store at the end of September, from 633,196 bales in brokers' stores at the end of June, was only half the increase of last season, it said.
Auction offerings were currently 24 percent higher than year-earlier levels, it said.
On sales from the stockpile, WI said unless prices increased significantly, sales in the second half of the season would barely exceed the proposed legislative quarterly minimum of 135,000 bales.
In this case, WI sales in 1996/97 would be about 14 percent lower than in 1995/96, it said.
Only a modest 36,936 bales were sold from WI stock in the five weeks to November 1.
Weekly sales averaged 50 percent less than in September at less than 7,400 bales, the lowest level since September 1995.
Low-level activity was attributed to subdued demand and WI's relatively good forward sold position at the start of the December 1996 quarter, it said.
